subject: Counterproposal request: structured ramp & SKU alignment
messages:
From: Ava Reynolds <ava.reynolds@cumuluspay.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Vendor comparison — follow up and ask for counterproposal

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We finished an internal evaluation and have a competing commercial offer on the table that materially changes the economics for our inference stack. They are offering a blended rate with a 12-month ramp that would drop our per-token cost by ~28% starting month 4, plus a free migration window.

Before we move forward, procurement asked whether Redwood can provide a formal counterproposal that:
- Aligns SKUs to our existing seat/instance naming (we need a simple mapping to our finance SKU catalog)
- Shows a structured ramp (month-by-month discounts tied to committed throughput)
- Includes any one-time migration credits or onboarding hours you can offer

Our baseline usage today: approx 2M generated tokens/month, spike months up to 3.8M. We expect growth to ~6M tokens/month over 12 months if price and performance are acceptable. We also require a 99.9% SLA and an option for private VPC deployment in Q4.

Can you send something by Friday (2026-05-22)? Procurement wants numbers and a short commercial term sheet to review.

Thanks,
Ava Reynolds
Head of Procurement — CumulusPay
ava.reynolds@cumuluspay.com

--
Note: Please treat the attached usage snapshot as confidential (sent in prior message).

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>

Folks — forwarding CumulusPay's ask. Key points: 2M baseline, ramp to 6M, need SKU mapping + structured ramp + migration credits. SLA 99.9% and private VPC option. They want something Friday.

My thinking: be pragmatic with a staged commit (quarterly commit increases), tie deeper discounts to AI-specific features (KV cache retention + prefix caching tier) rather than pure token discounts, and offer 120 hours of onboarding + two migration credits (egress/ingress assistance) in month 1.

Connor, can you draft the SKU mapping and confirm the VPC timeline? Jordan, can you price out a 9/6/3 month ramp structure (9-month baseline commit with 3-month optional step-down)? Marissa, need your take on discount cadence and approval for a one-time migration credit bucket.

Thanks — GR
Grace O'Connor

Subject: Re: Fwd: Vendor comparison — follow up and ask for counterproposal

All — I put numbers into the counterproposal spreadsheet (attached). High level:
- Offer A (Conservative): 12-month agreement, 2M committed tokens/mo, structured ramp to 5M by month 6. Effective blended per-token delta ≈ -15% vs list. Includes 80 hrs onboarding + $15k migration credit.
- Offer B (Aggressive): 24-month agreement, upfront commit for first 6 months (prepay bucket), ramp to 6M by month 4, blended delta ≈ -27% vs list (this closes the gap with their competitor). Includes 120 hrs onboarding + $30k migration credit + VPC scheduling priority in Q4.

Notes and tradeoffs: deep discounts require longer commitment (24mo) or upfront prepay; we should avoid over-indexing token discounts — recommend matching competitor's headline delta only for Offer B with a short-term pilot at 50% capacity so we limit risk.

Attachments: redwood_counterproposal_v2.xlsx (tab: commercial_summary), sku-mapping-overview.pdf

Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

On technicals: Connor, confirm whether offering prefix cache retention as a "feature-bundle" is feasible for CumulusPay's current model (they use long prefix contexts).

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-21T10:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Vendor comparison — follow up and ask for counterproposal

On 2026-05-21 Marissa Cole wrote:
> Notes and tradeoffs: deep discounts require longer commitment (24mo) or upfront prepay; we should avoid over-indexing token discounts — recommend matching competitor's headline delta only for Offer B with a short-term pilot at 50% capacity so we limit risk.

Agree with avoiding outright token cuts for Offer A. Technical calls: we can bundle an extended KV/prefix cache retention config as a part of the "feature-bundle" for Offer B — this will reduce per-token compute by offloading repeated context to cache and improve latency. That bundle is available without code changes; we would reserve the cache tier on their Dedicated pool. VPC in Q4 is doable but requires signed SOW and expected 6-week delivery once we kick off.

I'll attach a one-page tech note for the SKU mapping and the cache retention tiers. I recommend we include a 30-day pilot (pilot credits apply) to demonstrate perf delta.

Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.ai

Subject: Redwood counterproposal — structured ramp, SKU mapping, and migration credits (attached)

Hi Ava / Procurement team,

Appreciate the context — attached is a concise counterproposal (redwood_counterproposal_v2.xlsx) and a SKU mapping doc that aligns our runtime SKUs to your finance catalog (sku-mapping-overview.pdf). Summary of the recommended commercial path:

- Pilot (30 days): 50% capacity (limited to 1.5M tokens) with a $10k pilot credit.
- Offer B (recommended): 24mo term, phased ramp: months 1-3 at 2M commit, months 4-6 at 4M, months 7-24 at 6M committed. Blended commercial delta ≈ -25% vs our standard list; in month 4 onward economics approximate the competitor's headline delta.
- Migration/onboarding: 120 hrs of onboarding + $30k migration credit applied in month 1.
- Feature bundle: reserved KV/prefix cache tier for their Dedicated pool (improves per-token CPU by ~12–18% depending on repeat context).
- SLA: 99.9% with rollback clause to hosted API fallback if Dedicated is delayed beyond agreed timeline.

Next steps: If this aligns, we can circulate an MSA + SOW and a short DocuSign for the pilot credit within 48 hours. Please let us know by EOD Monday 2026-05-25 if you want Offer B spelled into a term sheet; otherwise we can move Offer A for a faster sign path.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow to walk the numbers.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
